answer:
The tallest fixed steel structure completed is the **Willis Tower** (formerly known as the Sears Tower) in Chicago, Illinois, USA. It was completed in **1973** or **1974**, with most reliable sources citing **1974** as the official completion year.

The Willis Tower stands at 442 meters (1,451 feet) to the roof and 527.0 meters (1,729 feet) including antennas. While the Burj Khalifa in Dubai is the tallest structure overall, it is not exclusively made of steel—it uses a combination of materials including reinforced concrete. Therefore, the Willis Tower remains recognized as the **tallest all-steel building**.
